evidence.title: A review of the impact of formative assessment on student achievement in mathematics
evidence.publisher: NOMAD Nordic Studies in Mathematics Education 22(3)
evidence.quote: The results show positive relations between student achievement in mathematics and the ways of doing formative assessment.
evidence.finding: Formative assessment is positively related to maths achievement, which supports the value of diagnosis but not that centres would pay for a tool.
evidence.limitation: Abstract-level; academic evidence on learning, not on purchasing by centres. Gap: Does not address primary-level diagnosis tools or purchasing by tuition centres.

evidence.title: Education Statistics Digest 2025, Section 1 Table 4
evidence.finding: There were 237,966 primary students in 2024; this is the context population, not the number of buyers.
evidence.limitation: Counts students, not paying buyers. Table 2 and Table 4 disagree (230,968 vs 237,966). Says nothing about tuition centres.

evidence.title: Singapore families spent S$1.8 billion on private tuition in 2023
evidence.publisher: Malay Mail (citing Straits Times / SingStat household expenditure survey)
evidence.quote: Families in Singapore reportedly spent S$1.8 billion (RM6 billion) on private tuition for their children in 2023
evidence.finding: Households spend heavily on private tuition, so centres have paying customers; it does not show centres would buy diagnostic software.
evidence.limitation: Secondary report; primary SingStat table not opened. All subjects and levels, not primary maths. Household spending on tuition, not centre spending on software.

evidence.title: Online Education in Singapore: How Geniebook Supports Academic Success
evidence.quote: AI-driven platforms like Geniebook tailor lessons based on students’ strengths and weaknesses, ensuring targeted improvement and better subject mastery.
evidence.finding: The text shows that Geniebook provides AI-driven personalized lessons targeting student strengths and weaknesses.
evidence.limitation: The quote does not explicitly state whether these reports are tutor-reviewed, evidence-traceable, or sold specifically to tuition centres.

evidence.title: The effect of a formative assessment practice on student achievement in mathematics
evidence.quote: The 14 teachers who participated in the PDP taught a total of 291 students (the intervention group). The students belonging to this group were 148 females and 143 males. The remaining 15 teachers (6 females, 9 males) that taught year-7 mathematics that school year taught a total of 275 students (the control group).
evidence.finding: The study evaluated mathematics achievement outcomes for 291 intervention students and 275 control students across participating secondary schools.
evidence.limitation: The study measures general secondary mathematics achievement rather than specifically diagnosing primary mathematics learning gaps.

evidence.title: Singapore's Education Ministry to deploy more AI in schools after success of primary 5 maths tool
evidence.quote: launched the Adaptive Learning System for mathematics, for three topics covered at the Primary 5 level. That followed a pilot involving 33 schools that began last year. uses machine learning to make customised learning recommendations for each student.
evidence.finding: The Singapore Education Ministry's Adaptive Learning System provides machine learning recommendations for primary mathematics students, but the text does not mention tutor-reviewed, evidence-traceable learning-gap reports sold to tuition centres.
evidence.limitation: The excerpt does not discuss commercial sales to tuition centres or whether reports are tutor-reviewed and evidence-traceable.

evidence.title: Online Education in Singapore: How Geniebook Supports Academic Success
evidence.quote: Parents receive detailed reports on their child’s strengths and areas for improvement, helping them provide timely support and keep learning on track.
evidence.finding: The platform provides detailed reports on strengths and areas for improvement directly to parents.
evidence.limitation: The text does not mention whether these reports are tutor-reviewed, evidence-traceable, or sold specifically to tuition centres.

evidence.title: 7-day work weeks, marking while at home: Singapore teachers say they're as busy as ever if not more
evidence.quote: For a class of 20, she typically prepares three different sets of learning materials to account for students of different abilities, which doubles preparation time.
evidence.finding: Differentiated learning and accommodating varying student ability levels in primary school classes requires preparing multiple sets of materials, doubling preparation time.
evidence.limitation: The quote discusses preparation time for differentiated learning in general rather than the specific process of diagnosing primary mathematics learning gaps.

evidence.title: Results from TALIS 2024: Singapore
evidence.quote: Full-time teachers report spending 6.4 hours per week on marking and correcting of student work (higher than the OECD average: 4.6).
evidence.finding: Full-time teachers in Singapore spend 6.4 hours per week marking and correcting student work, which indicates substantial time spent on assessment-related tasks.
evidence.limitation: The data reports overall marking and correcting time for teachers rather than specifically isolating primary mathematics or the diagnosis of learning gaps.
